correctness.rationale: Exact normalized weights follow from monomial differentiation/integration; degree-h finite differences with derivative truncation leave precisely one nonzero boundary column at order h+1. The polynomial leading coefficient of every lower r-th difference is nonzero and equals (-1)^r h!/(h-r)!, giving the sharp decreasing singular-value tail and endpoint membership. Matrix-unit density and invertible Vandermonde moments prove the closed span and generator minimality. CHECK.py passed 9008 finite tests; analytic proofs establish all infinite statements.

value.rationale: For a canonical family of noncompact critical integral operators, the theorem explicitly constructs rank-one finite differences, determines the minimal number of generators of any nonzero finite-rank combination, and classifies the exact norm-closed span. Every lower difference has a different sharp Schatten decay scale, yielding a complete spectral filtration rather than a trivial renaming or arbitrary finite example. This structural fact is useful for ideal-theoretic and approximation questions restricted to the natural fixed band.
